stories.headline: Anthropic raises $65B at $965B valuation, overtaking OpenAI as most valuable AI startup

key_facts.fact: Anthropic announced a $65 billion Series H financing at a $965 billion post-money valuation on Thursday, May 28.
The valuation pushes Anthropic above OpenAI, which was valued at $852 billion in late March after a record $122 billion round.
The round was led by Altimeter Capital, Dragoneer, Greenoaks and Sequoia Capital, and nearly triples Anthropic's $380 billion valuation from February.
Anthropic reported a $47 billion revenue run rate, up from a $30 billion run rate earlier this year and $10 billion in revenue last year, driven by its Claude Code coding assistant.
The round includes $15 billion of previously committed hyperscaler investments, including $5 billion from Amazon, with infrastructure partners such as Micron also contributing.

stories.headline: Anthropic adds dynamic workflows to Claude Code, fanning out hundreds of parallel subagents

key_facts.fact: Anthropic introduced dynamic workflows in Claude Code on May 28, where Claude writes orchestration scripts that run tens to hundreds of parallel subagents in a single session and checks its work before returning results.

Dynamic workflows launched in research preview across the Claude Code CLI, Desktop and VS Code extension for Max, Team and Enterprise plans, and on the Claude API, Amazon Bedrock, Vertex AI and Microsoft Foundry.

Anthropic cited the rewrite of Bun: Jarred Sumner used dynamic workflows to port Bun from Zig to Rust with 99.8% of the existing test suite passing, roughly 750,000 lines of Rust, in eleven days from first commit to merge.
The company said Claude Code with Opus 4.8 can now carry out codebase-scale migrations across hundreds of thousands of lines of code from kickoff to merge, using the existing test suite as its bar.
Anthropic warned that dynamic workflows can consume substantially more tokens than a typical Claude Code session and recommended starting on a scoped task.

stories.headline: Anthropic releases Opus 4.8, its most advanced model, tuned to flag its own uncertainty

key_facts.fact: Anthropic released Opus 4.8 on Thursday, May 28, calling it the newest version of its most advanced publicly available model, available everywhere at the same standard pricing as Opus 4.7.
The model arrived just 41 days after Opus 4.7, a much faster upgrade cycle than normal for Anthropic, amid pressure from new OpenAI Codex and Google Gemini Flash releases.
Anthropic's early testers found the new model is 'more likely to flag uncertainties about its work and less likely to make unsupported claims.'
A Bridgewater testimonial said the biggest difference was Opus 4.8's tendency to proactively flag issues with the inputs and outputs of an analysis that other models routinely missed.
Anthropic said it is still holding back its most advanced Mythos model over cybersecurity concerns but expects to bring Mythos-class models to all customers 'in the coming weeks.'

stories.headline: Apollo and Blackstone shop a $36B debt deal to buy Google TPUs for Anthropic to lease

key_facts.fact: Apollo Global Management and Blackstone are working to bring additional investors into a roughly $36 billion debt financing deal to help Anthropic build out its AI infrastructure.

The debt does not sit on Anthropic's balance sheet; it flows through a special-purpose vehicle that buys Google's custom TPUs and leases the hardware back to Anthropic for data centres in New York, Texas, Louisiana and Indiana.

Broadcom, which helps Google build the TPUs, is providing a residual-value support agreement on roughly $31 billion of the senior debt, effectively underwriting demand for its own chips if Anthropic stops paying and resale value falls short.

Investors were asked to submit orders this week with the deal expected to close the following week, in what could become one of the largest private credit deals in history and the biggest chip financing debt deal to date.
The TPUs serve as Anthropic's alternative to a Nvidia-only chip supply, and Apollo and Blackstone plan to sell down part of the debt while retaining significant portions themselves.

stories.headline: Blue Origin's New Glenn explodes in static-fire test, days before first Amazon Leo launch

key_facts.fact: A Blue Origin New Glenn first-stage booster nicknamed 'No, It's Necessary' exploded during a static fire test at Launch Complex 36, Cape Canaveral, shortly after 9 p.m. EDT on May 28, 2026.
The rocket was being prepared to launch 48 Amazon Leo broadband satellites as soon as the following week; the satellites were not aboard during the test.
The blast severely damaged the pad and toppled a lightning-protection tower; Space Launch Delta 45 reported no injuries or fatalities.
The FAA had cleared New Glenn to return to flight last week after investigating an April 19 upper-stage failure that left AST SpaceMobile's BlueBird 7 satellite in the wrong orbit.
Blue Origin said all personnel were accounted for after the 'anomaly,' and NASA Administrator Jared Isaacman pledged support for a thorough investigation.
LC-36 is the only launchpad built for the heavy-lift New Glenn and must be repaired before the rocket can return to flight.

stories.headline: BYD unveils Xuanji A3, which it calls China's most powerful ADAS chip, in smart-driving push

key_facts.fact: BYD unveiled the Xuanji A3, which it calls its most powerful ADAS (advanced driver assistance) chip yet, on May 28, 2026
The Xuanji A3 is the centerpiece of BYD's new laptop-sized central computing platform
BYD is the world's largest electric vehicle maker

stories.headline: Dell Q1 AI server revenue jumps 757% to $16.1B; raises FY27 AI server forecast to $60B

key_facts.fact: Dell reported Q1 fiscal 2027 total revenue of $43.84B, up 88% YoY, beating the $35.43B analyst estimate
AI server revenue was $16.1B, up 757% YoY
Dell booked $14.4B in AI server orders during the quarter, leaving a $20B remaining backlog
Dell raised its FY 2027 AI server revenue forecast to $60B, up from a prior projection of $50B
Dell shares jumped more than 38% in after-hours trading following the May 28 report

stories.headline: EU drafts emergency powers to override chip supply contracts during shortages

key_facts.fact: The EU is preparing sweeping emergency powers to intervene in Europe's chip supply chains during shortages
Under the draft law, chipmakers could be forced to override existing contracts and prioritize 'priority rated orders' during a declared crisis
The measure is part of a Chips Act 2.0 reform driven by concerns over dependence on Asian chip manufacturing

stories.headline: AI red-teaming startup Gray Swan raises $40M Series A at a $200M valuation

key_facts.fact: Pittsburgh-based Gray Swan, which stress-tests AI models for top frontier AI labs, raised a $40 million Series A at a $200 million valuation co-led by Wing VC and Madrona.
Gray Swan deploys an army of roughly 15,000 hackers to pressure-test models including Claude, GPT-5 and Gemini.
The company is raising as it expands beyond red-teaming for frontier labs to sell security tools to enterprises building AI agents.

stories.headline: IBM to invest $10B+ in quantum, targeting first large-scale fault-tolerant computer by 2029

key_facts.fact: IBM plans to invest more than $10B in quantum computing over five years
IBM aims to build the first large-scale, fault-tolerant quantum computer by 2029
The target system, IBM Quantum Starling, is expected to perform 20,000 times more operations than today's quantum computers
Starling will be housed in a new IBM Quantum Data Center in Poughkeepsie, New York, with investment largely focused on US-based manufacturing and research

stories.headline: IEA warns of 'largest energy security crisis ever' as Hormuz war reshapes investment

key_facts.fact: In its World Energy Investment 2026 report published Thursday, the IEA said the world is in 'the largest energy security crisis' in history as the Middle East war forces countries to scramble for new supply routes.

IEA chief Fatih Birol compared the situation to the structural changes triggered by the 1970s oil shocks, saying disruptions around the Strait of Hormuz have significantly changed global risk perceptions.
The IEA estimated global energy investment would rise to $3.4 trillion in 2026, while oil-production investment is expected to fall for a third consecutive year, slipping below $500 billion.
The crisis is accelerating investment in renewables, electricity grids, LNG, nuclear power and domestic energy sources as countries diversify away from imported fuels.

Birol separately warned Euronews that easing sanctions on Russian energy would be a 'major mistake'; turmoil in the Middle East has contributed to a 65% rise in oil prices and a more-than-doubling of gas prices, per European Commission estimates.

stories.headline: MediaTek taps Intel Foundry for advanced chip packaging, diversifying beyond TSMC

key_facts.fact: MediaTek says it has started working with Intel for advanced chip packaging, in addition to its existing relationship with TSMC
The Taiwan-based mobile chip designer is betting on AI demand for growth as it diversifies its packaging supply

stories.headline: OpenAI launches Rosalind Biodefense Program, offering its GPT-Rosalind model to trusted developers

key_facts.fact: OpenAI announced its Rosalind Biodefense Program, which will offer its GPT-Rosalind model for life sciences research to 'trusted developers' building biodefense tools.
OpenAI said it will sponsor access and provide launch support for epidemiological modeling, early detection, screening, preparedness, non-pharmaceutical interventions and other public-health work.
OpenAI said it briefed the White House and several federal agencies on its approach and is expanding access to GPT-Rosalind for select U.S. government and allied partners.

The program is part of a broader OpenAI biodefense push that includes backing startups, convening government officials, and a Preparedness Framework that enforces stricter safeguards as model biological capabilities rise.

stories.headline: Reactor exits stealth with $59M to build a platform for real-time generative video

key_facts.fact: Reactor emerged from stealth on May 28 with $59 million in funding led by Lightspeed Venture Partners, with participation from WndrCo, Amplify Partners, Sky9 Capital, FPV Ventures and others.
Reactor describes itself as the developer platform for real-time generative video, aiming to make real-time world models accessible to developers, and is headquartered in San Francisco.
The $59 million spans seed and Series A funding, with backers including former DreamWorks chief Jeffrey Katzenberg.

stories.headline: Samsung ships first 12-layer HBM4E memory samples, claiming early lead over SK Hynix and Micron

key_facts.fact: Samsung has begun shipping its first 12-layer HBM4E memory samples to customers
Samsung claims an early lead in shipping the industry's most advanced memory among the big three makers (Samsung, SK Hynix, Micron)
SK Hynix said in April it aimed to ship HBM4E samples in H2 2026

stories.headline: SpaceX lowers IPO valuation target to at least $1.8 trillion, down from $2T-plus

key_facts.fact: SpaceX is targeting a valuation of at least $1.8 trillion in its IPO, down from the $2 trillion-plus it sought as recently as April, after consultations with advisers and investors.
The company is seeking to raise as much as $75 billion, which would make it the biggest IPO of all time.
Roadshow marketing is expected to begin as soon as June 4, with pricing as early as June 11; the company plans to trade on Nasdaq under the symbol SPCX.
SpaceX reported $18.7 billion in 2025 revenue (up from $14 billion in 2024) but swung to a roughly $4.94 billion loss after acquiring xAI.
At $1.8 trillion, SpaceX would trade at roughly 96 times its 2025 revenue and rank among the world's most valuable companies, trailing only Apple, Nvidia, Microsoft and Alphabet.
Goldman Sachs, Morgan Stanley, Bank of America, Citigroup and JPMorgan are leading the IPO alongside 18 other banks, with an unusually large 30% retail-investor allocation.

stories.headline: Sweden to sell Ukraine up to 20 new Gripen E jets and donate 16 older C/D models

key_facts.fact: At a joint press conference at Uppsala Air Base on May 28, Sweden's PM Ulf Kristersson and Ukraine's President Volodymyr Zelensky said Ukraine intends to acquire an initial batch of up to 20 new Gripen E/F fighters and Sweden intends to donate up to 16 older Gripen C/D.
Ukraine plans to allocate 2.5 billion euros ($2.9 billion) from a 90 billion-euro EU support loan to fund the new aircraft.
The 16 donated Gripen C/D aircraft are due to be delivered in early 2027, while deliveries of the newer Gripen E are expected from 2030.
The deal builds on an October 2025 letter of intent for Ukraine to acquire up to 150 Gripen E jets, a purchase that would make Ukraine the world's second-largest Gripen operator by fleet size.
The donated aircraft come with weapons packages including missiles with a range exceeding 200 kilometers (124 miles).
Saab said it has not yet signed any contract nor received an order, with negotiations on Ukraine's Gripen E acquisition still to be completed.

stories.headline: US Q1 GDP revised down to 1.6% as sticky inflation cements no Fed cuts in 2026

key_facts.fact: US real GDP rose at a 1.6% annual rate in Q1 2026 (second estimate), revised down 0.4 percentage point from the advance estimate, versus a 0.5% increase in Q4 2025.
The downward revision primarily reflected weaker investment and consumer spending.
The Q1 PCE price index rose 4.5%, with the core PCE price index (excluding food and energy) up 4.4%, revised up 0.1 percentage point.
Corporate profits rose $40.4 billion in Q1, far below the $246.9 billion gain in Q4 2025.

The data and hawkish Fed remarks consolidated market expectations of no rate cuts in 2026; St. Louis Fed President Alberto Musalem warned that relying on future AI-driven productivity gains to tame inflation poses 'extremely high policy risks.'

stories.headline: Wix cuts about 1,000 jobs (20% of staff), CEO citing AI shift and strong shekel

key_facts.fact: Wix is laying off roughly 20% of its workforce — about 1,000 employees — in the largest round of cuts in the Israeli company's history, CEO Avishai Abrahami announced Thursday.
Wix had 5,277 employees at the end of Q1 2026, with more than 60% based in Israel.

Abrahami cited the rapid evolution of AI and a strengthening shekel, which has appreciated nearly 30% against the dollar over the past year to a 33-year peak, squeezing the mostly shekel-denominated cost base against dollar revenue.

Abrahami framed AI as a structural shift, writing it was 'the most significant shift in how companies are built since the invention of modern programming languages in the 1970s,' and said Wix will move to fewer management layers.
Wix shares have fallen nearly 50% since the start of the year; the company, once valued at around $20 billion, is now worth roughly $2 billion.
The company is reorganizing around AI-native roles such as 'Xengineer' and 'Creators' and is building its own AI model to power its Harmony website-building system.

stories.headline: UN climate agency: 75% chance the next five years breach 1.5C, smashing heat records

key_facts.fact: The World Meteorological Organization and UK Met Office project a 75% chance that the average global temperature in 2026-2030 will exceed 1.5C above pre-industrial levels, the Paris Agreement threshold.
There is a 91% chance at least one of the next five years individually breaches 1.5C, and an 86% chance one of them surpasses 2024's record as the hottest year ever measured.
The projection also forecasts the Arctic warming nearly 1.66C (3F) between now and 2030 and a dangerous drought with potential wildfires for the Amazon.
UN climate chief Simon Stiell called the report and Europe's heatwave a 'brutal reminder of the spiralling impacts of the climate crisis,' urging a faster shift to clean power.
The projections landed as a heat dome pushed record May temperatures across Europe and temperatures in Rajasthan, India hit 48.2C.
